messages.content: Explain how a language model produces text. Keep the answer under 100 words.

results.output: A language model generates text by predicting the most likely next word based on the input context. It uses patterns learned from vast amounts of training data to assign probabilities to possible word sequences. Starting with an initial prompt, the model selects words iteratively, updating the context with each choice. Advanced models like GPT use neural networks, specifically transformers, to process and understand relationships between words, enabling coherent and contextually relevant text generation. This process continues until a stopping condition, such as a specified length or end token, is met.

Input words are converted to embeddings, processed (commonly by transformer layers with attention) to produce a probability distribution over possible next tokens. Text is generated by repeatedly sampling or selecting the highest-probability token and feeding it back until a stopping condition is reached. Training adjusts weights to match real-world token patterns.
